questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'India's Contacts with the World' refers to.
questions.a: India has had continuous contacts with the world through trade, migration, religion and culture, connecting it with Central Asia, West Asia, Southeast Asia, China and Europe since ancient times.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'India's Contacts with the World'.
questions.a: India's location at the crossroads of Asia made it a hub of cultural and commercial exchange with distant civilisations.

questions.q: Under which section is 'India's Contacts with the World' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: India's Contacts with the World

concepts.title: Trade Routes -- Silk Route and Sea Routes

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Trade Routes -- Silk Route and Sea Routes' refers to.
questions.a: The Silk Route was an overland network connecting China to the Mediterranean through Central Asia, while sea routes across the Indian Ocean linked India to Arabia, East Africa and Southeast Asia.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Trade Routes -- Silk Route and Sea Routes'.
questions.a: India sat at the junction of the Silk Route and the Indian Ocean sea routes, making it a major centre of international trade.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Trade Routes -- Silk Route and Sea Routes' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Trade Routes

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Cultural Exchanges with the World' refers to.
questions.a: Cultural exchanges through trade and travel spread Indian art, architecture, language, science and literature to other regions, while India also absorbed ideas from Greece, Persia and Central Asia.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Cultural Exchanges with the World'.
questions.a: India both influenced and was influenced by other cultures, creating a rich two-way exchange of knowledge, art and ideas.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Cultural Exchanges with the World' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Cultural Exchanges

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Spread of Buddhism' refers to.
questions.a: Buddhism spread from India to Central Asia, China, Korea, Japan, Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia through the efforts of monks, traders and royal patrons like Emperor Ashoka.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Spread of Buddhism'.
questions.a: Buddhism was one of India's most important cultural exports, carried along trade routes by monks and merchants to large parts of Asia.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Spread of Buddhism' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Spread of Buddhism

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Indian Influence on Southeast Asia' refers to.
questions.a: Indian culture deeply influenced Southeast Asia through the spread of Hinduism, Buddhism, Sanskrit, the Ramayana and Mahabharata, temple architecture and the idea of kingship.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Indian Influence on Southeast Asia'.
questions.a: Indian influence shaped the art, language, religion and statecraft of Southeast Asian kingdoms like Funan, Srivijaya and the Khmer Empire.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Indian Influence on Southeast Asia' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Indian Influence on Southeast Asia

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Contacts with Greece and Rome' refers to.
questions.a: India had active trade and cultural contacts with the Greek and Roman civilisations, exchanging spices, textiles and gems for gold, wine and silver, and sharing ideas in science and art.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Contacts with Greece and Rome'.
questions.a: The Indo-Greek, Indo-Roman and Indo-Greek cultural contacts enriched both sides through trade and the exchange of knowledge, especially in art and astronomy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Contacts with Greece and Rome' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Contacts with Greece and Rome

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Medieval Trade and Indian Merchants' refers to.
questions.a: In medieval times, India continued to be a major trading power, with merchant guilds like the Manigramam and Ayyavole carrying trade across the Indian Ocean and to West Asia.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Medieval Trade and Indian Merchants'.
questions.a: Medieval Indian merchant guilds organised long-distance trade, financing voyages and maintaining trading posts across the Indian Ocean world.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Medieval Trade and Indian Merchants' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Medieval Trade

questions.q: Compute the travel time for a 2000 km voyage at a speed of 5 km per hour.. Use the method 'Computing Trade Distances and Times'. Work with: distance = 120, speed = 60. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of time_days.
questions.a: 0.0833 units

questions.q: How many days does a 960 nautical mile journey take at 4 knots (24 hours a day)? Use the method 'Computing Trade Distances and Times'. Work with: distance = 500, speed = 40. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of time_days.
questions.a: 0.5208 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Computing Trade Distances and Times' refers to.
questions.a: By estimating sailing speeds and distances between ports, we can compute the approximate time medieval ships took to travel between Indian and foreign ports.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Computing Trade Distances and Times'.
questions.a: Using the distance between ports and an assumed sailing speed, we can estimate how long trade voyages took in the medieval Indian Ocean.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Computing Trade Distances and Times', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: travel_time = distance / speed

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Impact of Global Connections' refers to.
questions.a: India's global connections shaped its economy, culture, religion and technology, bringing wealth through trade, spreading Indian culture abroad and bringing new ideas and techniques into India.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Impact of Global Connections'.
questions.a: India's long history of global contact made it both a giver and receiver of culture, enriching its civilisation and influencing many parts of the world.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Impact of Global Connections' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Impact of Global Connections

questions.q: Calculate the span between the opening of the Silk Route (c. 130 BCE) and Ashoka's missions (c. 250 BCE).. Use the method 'Timeline of India's Global Contacts'. Work with: year_1 = 25, year_2 = 1500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of centuries.
questions.a: 14.75 units

questions.q: How many years passed between Indo-Roman trade (c. 1st century CE) and the peak of the Khmer Empire (c. 12th century CE)? Use the method 'Timeline of India's Global Contacts'. Work with: year_1 = 25, year_2 = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of centuries.
questions.a: 4.75 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Timeline of India's Global Contacts' refers to.
questions.a: A timeline of India's global contacts spans from the ancient Silk Route (around 2nd century BCE) to medieval Indian Ocean trade, showing centuries of continuous exchange.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Timeline of India's Global Contacts'.
questions.a: By computing the span between key milestones we can see how long India's global connections have shaped its history.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Timeline of India's Global Contacts', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: time_span = later_year - earlier_year
